source_closure.common_header_reason: Two separate fixed guardian and leaf translation units share the single new private packet/identity helper header. No old runtime product, observer/CLI/controller entrypoint is loaded or executed; only captured-byte pure build/link/identity utility definitions may be reused.

fixed_topology.actual_process_tree: G guardian -> X preexec worker / E postexec same original PID -> D fixed descendant
fixed_topology.products: Two fresh separately compiled/linked ELF products: guardian and dedicated leaf. X starts as forked guardian product; fexecve transitions X to dedicated leaf E; E forks D once. D remains dedicated leaf product. No launcher, arbitrary command, additional exec/fork, service, respawn or foreign PID.
fixed_topology.assumption: G and outer observer/host survive throughout. Only these fixed owned roles under the trusted baseline are controlled.
fixed_topology.gate: G GET subreaper0, SET1, GET1 before any fork. X/E/D each actually GET0 at their stage; E explicitly rechecks after exec, not inferred. Unexpected state or failed call is negative.

identity_product_transition.G: G capture independently agrees with observer direct-childPID/parentPID/UID and freshly bound guardian product.
identity_product_transition.preexec: G forks X once, closes parent unused endpoints, binds G_E with before/after identity, fdinfo and live poll. X PRE_EXEC_READY identifies its own G product, expected G parent, birth/boot/UID, t0/nonce/case and FD flags. G independently checks before authorizing EXEC.
identity_product_transition.postexec: Only X product may transition from exact guardian tuple to exact dedicated-leaf tuple. PID/start/boot/UID/EUID/PPID remain equal. G_E is same original handle acquired preexec, rechecked live postexec and never reopened/reset. E POST_EXEC_READY is accepted only together with exec-error writer EOF, actual leaf startup FD facts and independent G /proc identity and product observation. EOF alone is not successful exec.
identity_product_transition.descendant: G explicitly sends CREATE_D only after postexec validation. E creates child pipes then forks D once, anchors E_D after fork, verifies before/after identity/fdinfo/live facts. D READY is forwarded unchanged by E, G independently checks D.PPID=E, boot/UID/leaf tuple and binds G_D before ARM.
identity_product_transition.adoption: Only worker_loss permits D.PPID E->G, after E terminal and exact G wait E/raw9. G independently rereads same D birth/boot/UID/leaf product, its own current identity and live pidfd before G_D signal and adopted-child wait. Raw wait/signal/pidfd terminal alone never proves adoption.
identity_product_transition.limit: Product tuple plus Python returned hash is controlled-source identity evidence, not immutable inode bytes, whole mapped-code authentication, parent/whole-ancestry authentication, node alias or physical exclusion.

exec_interface.signature: Use fexecve(int fd, char *const argv[], char *const envp[]) declared by fresh reviewed unistd.h with _GNU_SOURCE. Do not guess architecture, SYS_execveat number or libc backend.
exec_interface.descriptor: G opens only freshly linked fixed leaf path once with O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC|O_NOFOLLOW, fstat bounded regular ELF exact product tuple, and duplicate with F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC as a named witness. In X both stay CLOEXEC and fstat must still equal. X fexecve original leafFD once after EXEC; return (including EINTR/ENOENT/EBADF) means permanent negative exec error; no retry, alternative path/interpreter, old product or command.
exec_interface.argv: Exact finite strings: fixed program-name/frontier-owned-leaf marker, --fixed-leaf, case enum, nonce64hex, decimal shared t0, G PID/birth/UID, boot36, exact command-read/report-write fd numbers, leafFD/witnessFD/exec-error-writerFD numbers and expected two product tuples. Strict arity/parsing/finite bounded representations, no user command/path/argv.
exec_interface.environment: Exact envp {NULL}; no inherited PATH, LD_*, Python, shell or credentials. Trusted libc/loader may internally choose fexecve implementation; no claim of a measured direct kernel exec backend.
exec_interface.error_pipe: pipe2(O_CLOEXEC), G retains read and X retains CLOEXEC writer. X failure writes one bounded EXEC_ERROR fact then closes and _exit(71). EOF after successful exec is necessary but insufficient. G must retain missing/partial error frame, timeout and actual direct-child terminal evidence as negative.
exec_interface.CLOEXEC_startup: Leaf first application FD operations, before any open/proc reads, separately F_GETFD leafFD/witnessFD/error-writerFD and require -1/EBADF. These mean named original handles are gone at application entry; FD-number reuse later is a new identity. Command-read/report-write each must be live with observed F_GETFD flags lacking FD_CLOEXEC and distinct from the three closed numbers. They are the only private descriptors retained across exec. Dynamic loader startup occurred before main; no claim of uninterrupted FD-number vacancy or full loader closure.
exec_interface.failed_exec: No descendant has yet been authorized or created. X closes known own descriptors once, exits71; G bounds observation and reaps only its own X if terminal/identity known. No planned or negative signal. No success-shaped product transition can override the saved exec error.

FD_protocol.initial: All pipe ends start pipe2(O_CLOEXEC). X explicitly closes unrelated parent endpoints and its inherited stdio copies before PRE_EXEC_READY; G is sole final JSON stdout writer. G_E is opened after fork and never inherited. Only X command-read/report-write have FD_CLOEXEC cleared with exact F_GETFD/F_SETFD/F_GETFD facts before fexecve. Managed FD ledger refers to named private pipe/product/pidfd handles only. G inherited stdin/stdout/stderr remain separate; G final stdout stays open through actual JSON output, with no fabricated postclose/EBADF or final stdout closure gate. X original stdio copies are explicit preexec-child-only closes, separately named by original handle/epoch. D has no inherited original stdio handles: all three original-stdio slots are absent/unattempted with null close/result/errno/EBADF facts. D must never close a number merely because it is0/1/2. The preexec X gate requires its five exec descriptor numbers distinct from original stdio0/1/2; this is not a restriction on new postexec child pipe numbers.
FD_protocol.exec_witness: G explicitly once-closes its leaf/witness/error-writer copies after fork, preserving original identities. X leaf/witness/error-writer closure across successful exec has first-leaf EBADF plus parent error EOF, not invented explicit close returns.
FD_protocol.descendant: E creates four new child endpoints only after CREATE_D. D closes both unrelated E-G endpoints and child parent-side copies before READY. E closes child-side copies. E_D/G_D opened only after D fork. No inherited ancestor pidfd.
FD_protocol.normal: D consumes FINISH only after ARM and reports command-read close/immediateEBADF in FINISH_ACK, then closes sole report writer and exits0. E observes exact ACK and EOF, polls/waits D/raw0, closes E_D once/immediateEBADF, closes own remaining child endpoints, then closes G command-read before final E_FINISH_ACK and report writer/exit0. A writer cannot report its own post-close result over that same writer; parent EOF/exit is distinct evidence, never fabricate explicit close/EBADF.
FD_protocol.loss: D remains alive on E-command EOF after worker loss and parks to absolute expiry, without premature exit or signal. E_D and E-owned pipe teardown after SIGKILL are kernel owner-death facts only; no explicit-close/EBADF values invented. G-owned G_E/G_D and all G pipe endpoints explicitly once-close/immediateEBADF. D treats loss EOF as expected park, sends no error to the killed E reader. PIPE EOF does not prove ancestor terminal/adoption; G uses its independent wait/adoption facts.
FD_protocol.handle_labels: Original FD handle ledger is keyed by owner/semantic label/acquisition epoch; descriptor integer reuse never resets signal or close budget. Close exactly once, even uncertain EINTR outcome: preserve fact, never retry.

generation_aliasing.original_stdio_epoch: X records original inherited stdio descriptors0/1/2 onceclose/immediateEBADF before PRE_EXEC_READY/fexecve. E application entry has those original handles absent. Dynamic loader/app temporary descriptor reuse remains outside a continuous vacancy claim.
generation_aliasing.new_child_epoch: After validated POST_EXEC_READY/CREATE_D, E pipe2 may lawfully return0/1/2. These are new named E-D endpoints with independent provenance, not old stdio. D retains its exact child-command-read/report-write and closes only other explicitly known inherited endpoint labels/epochs, including unrelated E-G endpoints. No broad close(0),close(1),close(2) or close-range rule based on integer labels.
generation_aliasing.evidence: Ledger includes semantic label/owner/acquisition epoch/actual FD for every managed handle. D originalstdio generation slots absent/unattempted, result/errno/EBADFnull; any D close of new FD0/1/2 is recorded solely under its actual private-endpoint generation. Original FD integer reuse never restarts signal/close budget. Descriptor0 is legal in parser and fixtures.
generation_aliasing.fixture: Portable fixtures must include legal postexec E-D endpoint reuse0/1/2 with absent D-originalstdio facts and preserve private frames; reject duplicate provenance or stdio-close ledger claiming closure of a retained child endpoint.

packet_protocol.format: New common-header private fixed frame <=512 bytes, _Static_assert <=PIPE_BUF and runtime fpathconf(_PC_PIPE_BUF)>0. Captured compiler machine bounds must agree for both products. Each exact full frame binds schema/magic/kind/role/case/nonce/sharedt0/edge ordinal/target identity; use finite bounded payloads, no whole final JSON forwarding.
packet_protocol.reads: Bounded poll/read/write with positive monotonic deadlines and exact framing. Partial/missing/duplicate/malformed/out-of-order/unknown frames and EINTR errors are negative; no signal or exec retry. A partial read may accumulate remaining frame bytes as framing, not restart a failed operation. Private pipe endpoints use O_NONBLOCK in addition to CLOEXEC, with fresh deadline-gated poll then exact bounded atomic write; EAGAIN/EPIPE/EINTR syscall errors are negative, no write retry. Read framing may accumulate successful partial reads under the same absolute deadline. Local SIGPIPE disposition is deliberately SIG_IGN via reviewed sigaction before any private writes, with actual success/error facts; it is a process-local disposition, not a directed signal. Exec preserves ignored dispositions under trusted ABI, and E explicitly checks/sets its required local disposition before later packet writes. Bounded ERROR writes are best effort, never a guarantee of complete output.
order: G_E bound live and EXEC G
D READY + E_D facts forwarded by E
packet_protocol.forwarding: D identity/FD/ACK/wait-independent facts retain original role/nonce/sequence while E transports them as individually tagged frames. Per-source-role/per-direction sequences are checked, with explicit forwarding transport/source distinction. No duplicate action grant or counts inferred from file existence.

pidfds.acquisition: symbolic SYS_pidfd_open flags0, per-original target birth/boot/UID/product live before/after plus fdinfo targetPID and F_GETFD flags; no free-PID kill fallback.
pidfds.combined: Each original G handle has combined planned+negative attempts <=1; actual negative signal attempts=0 in every case. Consume before one syscall(SYS_pidfd_send_signal, fd, SIGKILL, NULL, 0). Any failure/EINTR/ESRCH/unknown consumes budget, immediately disables every later planned signal including unattempted D; no new-handle/FD-number budget reset. No E/D directed signals. Exact G_E work5 and G_D cleanup8 gates are required immediately before each syscall, after fresh identity/live checks; terminal10 or final12 checks never retroactively authorize a late call.
pidfds.waits: G_E direct child G can wait only original X/E; normal E waits original direct D, G never waits D; loss G may wait D only after observed adoption. Fixed waitpid(original_pid,WNOHANG) loops record poll attempts/actual one successful reap, not fictitious single total invocation. No wait(-1), process-group killing or unrelated reap.

budgets_negative_terminal.t0: G one CLOCK_MONOTONIC before fork; strictly finite positive int64ns, checked addition overflow, inherited X and exact argv E then D. Monotonic nondecreasing observations per role, nondecreasing globally required causal boundaries. No guessed realtime equivalence.
budgets_negative_terminal.error: First local observed error permanently disables new EXEC/CREATE_D/ARM/FINISH and all planned signals. Propagate bounded ERROR fact if writer still owned/live; once G sees failure it sends no further action. Do not claim instantaneous distributed cancellation of commands already sent before error. Negative_cleanup_signals empty0.
budgets_negative_terminal.allowed_negative: Only bounded identity/poll/FD/error observations, proper direct-child or explicitly observed adopted-child wait, known-own original handle once-close, best-effort bounded error frames, fixed _exit failure/self-expiry. No new fork/exec/ARM/cleanup signal/retry/fallback. Preserve created/bound/adopted/terminal/reaped/unknown role sets; no defaults for unobserved syscall outcomes.
budgets_negative_terminal.roles: X fexecve-return failure writes bounded EXEC_ERROR if possible, closes known-own FDs once and immediately _exit(71), no D ever created. E no-D startup/FD leak/identity failure writes bounded ERROR if possible, once-closes any known still-open owned witness/private FDs and immediately _exit(70); G observes its own E poll/wait under terminal10/G12 and retains actual incomplete failure if not reaped. No reset or narrow success on either negative. After D is actually created, E/D command/protocol/error paths may only close/observe/legitimate-parent-wait then park to childexpiry14/_exit(non-success); G stops at12 and never reports later expiry as observed. In planned worker_loss, D receives expected E-command EOF, closes known-own endpoints once and parks without sending ERROR to dead E and without autoexit/signal before fixed14.
budgets_negative_terminal.reset: Only if no error, correct case wait owners/statuses, every created E/D proven terminal/reaped, all G own FD predicates complete and event times<terminal10/Gtotal12: G SET0 once and GET0. Unknown/unreaped negative never resets. SET/GET failure or post-reset clock error prevents success; accurately retain partial reset fact with error; no setter retry, queue/global restore claim.
budgets_negative_terminal.outer: Observer/compiler direct-child timeout bounds outer activity only, cannot guarantee all descendants gone after outer/G/host loss. Negative case may leave self-expiring orphan beyond G12; no full containment or cleanup promise.

Failed/late/unknown clock gate consumes no uncalled signal but permanently disables all later actions. A called signal consumes original budget before entry and cannot retry regardless of return.
